why_trail.why: Handoff complete on all seven fields. No docs/agents/CREW_CONTEXT.md or GLOSSARY.md in this repo, so crew doctrine is global-only. Grounded read-only against C:/Programs/f1Brainz/docs/architecture/: the anchor token-scan regex yields 0 ids on skills/cartographer/templates/ARCHITECTURE_INDEX.template.md (so the shipped template correctly reads DEGRADED) and 76 unique ids on f1Brainz index.md / 58 on packets/physics.md. Independently confirmed the handoff's parse_packet claim: build_architecture_map.parse_packet raises MapBuildError 'missing required field: structural node' on all 16 f1Brainz packets (0 parsed / 16 failed) because f1Brainz uses YAML fences while this repo's template uses bold fields - so coupling to the strict parser would return zero nodes on the ONE repo with a real map.

scripts/map_orient.py written. Frozen exit table 0/10/11/12/13 sits strictly above argparse(2) and traceback(1) and strictly below 126/127, so no verdict can be confused with a mistyped flag, a crash, or a missing POSIX shell. Pure decision layer (scan_anchors, candidate_is_citable, candidate_outcome, prove_repo_root, determine_mode, build_orientation, classify_*, exit_code_for, build_receipt, render_orient_report) is separated from the impure edges (probe_root/git_toplevel/collect_candidates/write_receipt/pin_substitutes/_now_iso). --self-test = 45 checks, green. Live run against this repo prints DEGRADED-NO-MAP and exits 10 (reported, not silent). Grounded read-only against f1Brainz through the pure path: RESOLVED, entrypoint docs/architecture/index.md, 76 anchors, and the packets-dir candidate is STILL recorded after index.md hit, proving the delivery-record property. Gotcha found: importlib-loaded modules need sys.modules[name]=module before exec_module or frozen dataclasses raise on 3.14 - the test loader must do this.

TDD red genuinely observed: tests/test_map_orient.py written BEFORE verify-orientation and the discharge predicates existed, run gave '24 failed, 28 passed, 9 subtests passed' - every failure in the verify-orientation/partial-fill/hash-pin arms plus one wrong expected anchor count I then corrected (4 not 5). Then implemented is_filler/substitutes_declared/unmapped_declared/escalation_declared/degraded_record_is_complete (the pinned all)/missing_degraded_fields/receipt_problems/verify_verdict/render_verify_report + the verify-orientation subcommand + orient's --substitute/--unmapped/--escalation declaration flags with sha256 hash-pinning. Green: 42 passed, 22 subtests passed. One correction found while implementing: an UNRESOLVABLE-ROOT receipt legitimately has an EMPTY candidates_tried (we never looked), so the well-formedness check exempts that mode only - otherwise a truthful could-not-look receipt would verify as 12 receipt-unusable instead of 11.

<repo-root> added to resolve_spine and to _RESOLVER_OWNED_TOKEN_RE. DEVIATION from the handoff's literal 'str(Path(root).resolve())': emitted as Path(root).resolve().as_posix(). Evidence - a spine is JSON and instantiate_spine json.loads() its own output, so a Windows str(Path) value 'C:\Programs\...' makes that guard raise 'Invalid \escape', proven by direct run; as_posix() parses fine and is also correct for the POSIX shell the engine runs command checks under. Justification comment says ROBUSTNESS (checks receive no cwd and inherit the launcher's; the five shipped relative checks are fragile, not broken, and are left alone per #341). SCOPE STRETCH: added a 5-test RepoRootPlaceholder class to tests/test_init_work_area.py, which the allowed-scope list did not name, because the handoff's required-evidence command runs that file and an untested placeholder is not shippable. tests/test_init_work_area.py 31 passed (26 before + 5 new). Falsifiability spot-checked: mutating the resolver back to str(Path(...)) makes the json-safe test go red.

tests/test_mutation_floor.py: 7 passed, 4 subtests. The applied-assertion runs FIRST and is a strict count delta, not an 'in' check: original.count(old)==1, mutated.count(old)==0, mutated.count(new)==original.count(new)+1. The delta form matters here concretely - mutation 2's replacement '    return EXIT_OK' ALREADY appears elsewhere in the module, so an 'assertIn' would have passed even if nothing was substituted. apply_mutation raises a dedicated HarnessError naming 'NOT a killed mutant' when an anchor matches 0 or >1 times, and two HarnessSelfCheck tests prove that path fires. Unmutated baseline asserted green first. Each kill additionally requires (a) passed_count>0 so a broken import cannot count as a kill and (b) a FAILED node in the class the mutation was supposed to break. Measured: all->any exit 1, 36 still passing, 9 killers incl. all six PartialFillMatrix arms; UNRESOLVABLE-ROOT collapse exit 1, 33 passing, 11 killers incl. both CouldNotLookDiscriminator tests; citability->existence exit 1, 32 passing, 10 killers incl. test_the_shipped_index_template_itself_does_not_resolve.

Required evidence captured verbatim into .agent-work/issue-304/crew-handoffs/g1-result.md: the 80-passed three-file suite, self-test OK, the live DEGRADED-NO-MAP orient run with exit 10 plus its receipt and the verify-orientation refusal, the per-mutation kill table, and the 1459-passed full-suite regression check. Exit table 0/10/11/12/13 stated with the collision argument. Three deviations declared: as_posix() instead of str(Path) for <repo-root> with the json.loads evidence; the additive scope stretch into tests/test_init_work_area.py; and orient's three declaration flags beyond the frozen synopsis. Three triage candidates and honest workflow feedback recorded.
